title: Canonizer after prefix extraction
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean words. After exactly $3|\alpha|+4$ steps of the prefix-parser–canonizer composition on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, the configuration has the canonizer in its initial configuration on input $\alpha$, its input head at position $2|\alpha|+3$, and its boundary tag true. The prefix parser’s work tapes are blank with their heads at zero, and the composition’s buffer stores $\alpha$ with its head at position zero; the output is empty.
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean
strings. Starting the buffered composition of the doubled-bit prefix parser and $c$’s
canonizer on the paired input $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, after exactly $3|\alpha|+4$
steps its configuration is the buffered second-phase configuration in which the
canonizer is in its initial configuration on input $\alpha$, the virtual-boundary flag
is true, and the physical input head is at position $2|\alpha|+3$.
